correctness.rationale: The EFX singleton/pair criterion is necessary and sufficient by direct removal of either paired good; nonnegative monotone valuations make the reverse envy vacuous. Refined strict favorites reduce all possible value vectors to agreement/disagreement on the first two singleton reports. In the agreement case at least two of four equally likely assignment prefixes have a valid completion; in the disagreement case at least one of two equally likely prefixes has one. The third assignment uses only revealed singleton values. Two additive witness matrices have the same first-arrival report yet require opposite recipients of the first good in every EFX allocation. Direct finite verification checked 4096 weak-value additive pairs, 36 strict-ranking pairs, 729 nonadditive max-singleton pairs, and both 8-pattern upper witnesses. Computation is corroborating, not the universal proof.

value.rationale: This determines the exact minimax success probability at the first nontrivial market size in the n+1-good family, closing a genuine published 1/3-versus-1/2 gap. The policy exploits minimal observable ordinal information, and the lower argument extends beyond additive utilities to every normalized nonnegative monotone set valuation. The constant quantifies finite-horizon EFX feasibility for randomized online allocators; the result is not a vacuous normalization check or an arbitrary empirical slice.
